PROFILE: Physician-scientist and translational researcher in maternal and child health. I develop and validate predictive and diagnostic tools and interventions that can be deployed at public-health scale to reduce adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth, fetal growth restriction and the great obstetrical syndromes, through robustly designed cohort studies, randomised trials and secondary analyses of pooled national data. I am an investigator in the Interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on Birth Outcomes - DBT India Initiative (GARBH-Ini), where I work with multi-omics and data-science teams to discover biomarkers and build AI-driven clinical decision tools, and I have translated this work into four Indian patent applications (three awarded). During 2020-2023 I coordinated the clinical research component of the DBT Consortium for COVID-19 Research, including the real-world effectiveness evaluation of COVID-19 vaccines that informed national immunisation policy. I currently lead, as Principal Investigator, two ICMR National Health Research Priority (NHRP) projects on hypothyroidism in pregnancy and gestational weight gain, and I am Co-Principal Investigator of the ICMR-funded GRASPP randomised controlled trial and the Gates Foundation-supported MOMI-India consortium.
SHORT_BIO_100: Dr Ramachandran Thiruvengadam is a physician-scientist and translational researcher with interests in the development and validation of biomarkers and AI-driven clinical decision tools for pregnancy outcomes. He is an Associate Professor at the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Department of Biotechnology, Government of India, and an investigator in the Interdisciplinary Group for Advanced Research on Birth Outcomes - DBT India Initiative (GARBH-Ini). As part of this programme, he has worked closely with multi-omics experts to discover novel biomarkers for preterm birth and other pregnancy outcomes.
